trial_court: Sub Court, Karunagappally in O.S No.318/2012; Additional District Court - IV, Kollam in A.S No.3/14
case_name: Shylaja Beegum @ Shylaja Babu vs Anoop A on 3 November, 2025

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Shylaja Beegum @ Shylaja Babu (wife), Athira S.Babu (daughter), Arathi S.Babu (daughter)
parties.respondent_defendant: Anoop A (son of Babu Vijayanath), State represented by Secretary to Government, Commissioner for Rural Development, District Collector, Asst. Development Commissioner (General), Tahsildar, Block Development Officer

facts_of_case: The plaintiff claims to be the only son of Babu Vijayanath who passed away under suspicious circumstances. The plaintiff seeks declaration regarding his status and setting aside a legal heirship certificate.

legal_principles.principle: The court cannot pick stray sentences from oral testimony to hold that a marriage was not solemnized in accordance with the provisions of the Hindu Marriage Act.
legal_principles.held: It is further submitted that prior to the marriage, there was an agreement between late Babu Vijayanath and the 1st appellant, which was later preceded by the customary ceremonies. As regards the finding of the trial court on the alleged admission made by the 1 st defendant in her cross examination, the learned counsel pointed out that it was not possible for the courts below to have picked some stray sentences from her oral testimony to hold that the marriage was not solemnized in accordance with the provisions of the Hindu Marriage Act.

legal_principles.principle: The court must appreciate the oral and documentary evidence before rendering a decision.
legal_principles.held: On appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence, relied on the statement made by the 1st defendant/appellant herein in her cross examination that, at the time of marriage, she had not converted herself to Hindu religion and even after the marriage she continued to be a Muslim and did not convert to Hindu religion.

outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed, and the judgment of the trial court is set aside.
